transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-11-07
Start time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Park (Redwood AE), Ravi Kapoor (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Ridgeview Head of ML), Samir Patel (Ridgeview Platform Engineer), Olivia Torres (CTO)

Auto-generated summary (optional):
- Walkthrough of Console usage lenses and per-route cost playbook.
- Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted for Ridgeview's low-latency patient-facing API.
- Security/SSO and VPC questions surfaced; Redwood to share docs and benchmark process.

Topics: usage lanes, per-route dashboards, cost breakdown, batching & caching, dedicated capacity, SOC2/KMS/VPC

Transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate it. Uh, we're gonna walk through the Console usage lanes and a per-route cost playbook that we've been using for customers with similar patterns to Ridgeview. Ravi and I will tag-team it.
[00:20] Maya Chen: Hi all, thanks. Quick note — we have the product and infra folks here so we can go deep, um, so feel free.
[00:31] Ravi Kapoor: Cool. I'll start with a quick UI tour and then we'll drill into the per-route telemetry and where the cost numbers come from.
[00:40] Samir Patel: Quick question — timeline-wise we need a pilot by mid-November if possible, otherwise the Q1 budget signoff slips.
[00:48] Jamie Park: Noted, Samir. We'll put pilot kickoff in the next steps.
[00:54] Ravi Kapoor: Opening the console — first screen is the Usage Lenses view, think of it as a high-level rollup. You can slice by model, route, time window, and then drill into route-level dashboards.
[01:12] [01:12] Olivia Torres: Sorry, I can't quite see — are these 'routes' the API endpoints we define or are they user journeys?
[01:20] Jamie Park: Good callout. In Redwood, routes are logical endpoints you register — they map to your API paths or internal workflow identifiers. So you can have /patient-summary as a route and it will surface token counts, latency percentiles and cost per request.
[01:39] Maya Chen: And how is cost calculated per request? We need to reconcile that with our internal billing.
[01:46] Ravi Kapoor: Short answer: per-token compute cost + model variant multiplier + infra amortization for Dedicated. The console shows a normalized unit cost and then expands to raw GPU-seconds and token counts.
[02:05] Jamie Park: There's also cache hit crediting: if you enable prefix/KV caching, the dashboard shows effective cost after cache savings. That tends to be a big lever for patient-facing repeated prompts.
[02:25] [02:25] Samir Patel: Our traffic is 75% short prompts under 64 tokens but 25% long summaries. Does the console give distribution by sequence length?
[02:36] Ravi Kapoor: Yup, sequence-length heatmaps and the per-route histogram. You can filter to see how much spend is coming from >512 token tails.
[02:47] Maya Chen: Nice. Okay, show us how to compare Hosted vs Dedicated economics.
[02:52] Ravi Kapoor: Switching to the Route Cost Comparison tab — we compare cost per 1M requests across hosting modes for that route. For Dedicated we show committed capacity amortized, peak latency SLOs, and burst costs. You can overlay expected savings if you enable quantization profiles or batching.
[03:14] Olivia Torres: When you say "quantization profiles" — any impact on quality? We can't have hallucination regressions in clinical outputs.
[03:23] Jamie Park: Right — we surface quality regressions in the Optimize tab. You can run eval sets against model+quantization combos and see score deltas. For clinical flows we recommend conservative 8-bit quantization and acceptance gating via evals.
[03:43] Samir Patel: Security — SAML SSO, audit logs, and KMS for keys are musts. We're in an environment that needs to keep PHI within our VPC.
[03:53] Ravi Kapoor: Understood. Redwood Private supports a customer-managed control plane or on-prem package. We integrate with customer KMS and HSM for key management; audit logs are exportable to your SIEM. We'll share the SOC2/ISO paperwork.
[04:10] Maya Chen: Can the console show cost attribution by team or product line? We have cross-functional teams using the same model.
[04:18] Jamie Park: Yes — our route tagging and token attribution let you map routes to teams and then roll up cost by tag. There's a chargeback export you can drop in your billing system.
[04:30] [04:30] Ravi Kapoor: I'm going to demonstrate a live example — here's /patient-summary route, last 30 days. You can see token-level breakout, average latency p50/p95/p99, error rates, and a cost-per-request timeline.
[04:50] Maya Chen: I see a spike — what's that?
[04:53] Ravi Kapoor: That's a batch job hitting the route at 03:00 UTC. Console flags anomalous bursts and suggests candidate policies: schedule a separate route for batch or apply a different priority class so it doesn't affect latency SLO.
[05:10] Samir Patel: How does Redwood handle intelligent routing? Like route low-priority to cheaper model at the edge?
[05:18] Jamie Park: We have routing policies: you can route by latency target, cost cap, region, or customer tier. For example, you can set non-critical routes to fall back to a lower-cost model variant or quantized profile when latency is relaxed.
[05:33] Olivia Torres: About observability — do we get token-level traces back to our logs? We want to correlate an inference with our request IDs.
[05:41] Ravi Kapoor: Yes, there's request-level tracing if you pass your request id header; it will appear in the trace view. You can export traces to Datadog or our tracing hooks.
[05:53] Maya Chen: Can you show the Optimize recommendations? We wanna see how Redwood suggests batching settings.
[05:59] Ravi Kapoor: Jumping to Optimize — it recommends batch sizes based on observed sequence length distributions and target p95 latency. It shows estimated cost saved and projected impact on latency. For /patient-summary it suggests 4–8 concurrent batching for our token distribution, saving about 18% cost, but with a slight bump in p95 — you can tune to hit your SLO.
[06:28] [06:28] Jamie Park: Also, the console simulates cost if you change quantization or enable caching. That plan view is handy for finance reviews.
[06:38] Samir Patel: For the pilot we'd like to run a per-route benchmark with our payloads — can Redwood run that or do we run it?
[06:46] Ravi Kapoor: We can run it on our side or give you a runner. For Dedicated pilots we usually run a brief benchmark in both Hosted and Dedicated to validate p95 and unit cost. We'll need sample traffic traces and SLO targets.
[07:00] Maya Chen: We'll share sample traces. Also need to know data retention for logs — retention horizon and encryption at rest.
[07:08] Jamie Park: Logs can be retained per your config; for Private deployments you control retention. All data at rest is encrypted; we support customer-managed keys. We'll attach the security whitepaper.
[07:22] Olivia Torres: Any limitations around on-prem? We have some batches that need to run isolated in our network.
[07:28] Ravi Kapoor: On-prem package supports air-gapped deployment. There are some ops prerequisites, but we've done it with a handful of regulated customers. We'll put the installation checklist in the follow-up.
[07:39] [07:39] Samir Patel: Competitors — we looked at ModelServeCo and Anthropic — what differentiates Redwood on the cost side?
[07:47] Jamie Park: Two big things: the unified runtime that lets you apply policies and the cost tooling — per-route attribution, simulated cost changes, and Optimize recommendations. Today that gives teams predictable cost reductions without building custom telemetry pipelines.
[08:05] Maya Chen: Any caveats for clinical accuracy when using caching? Could caching return stale info?
[08:12] Ravi Kapoor: Cache semantics are configurable. For patient-facing data you can scope cache to non-sensitive prompt prefixes and set TTLs. Also, we support cache invalidation hooks if you have content that must be fresh.
[08:29] Olivia Torres: Great. Walk me through the billing export — teams want CSV with cost by route and tag.
[08:36] Jamie Park: The Billing Export feature lets you schedule daily exports with route, tag, model, raw tokens, effective cost, and Azure/GCP/AWS cost breakdown if you're on Dedicated with cloud infra pass-through.
[08:51] Samir Patel: On Dedicated, do we commit per-GPU or per-throughput? We need predictable throughput for peak clinic hours.
[08:59] Ravi Kapoor: You commit to throughput buckets and GPU types. The console shows provisioning suggestions based on historical traffic. We also support autoscaling policies within your commit and controlled burst capacity.
[09:14] [09:14] Maya Chen: Show the canary rollout for model changes — how would we validate a new model variant without affecting production?
[09:22] Ravi Kapoor: We have canary and A/B rollouts. You can route X% of traffic to a new variant, capture eval metrics, and automatically rollback on regressions. Rollout policies can be tied to your eval suites and SLO gates.
[09:38] Jamie Park: Important note: we integrate with your CI to run evals as part of the deployment pipeline, so rollouts are automated once tests pass.
[09:48] Olivia Torres: If we sign up for Dedicated pilot, can we have an on-call hand from Redwood for the initial week?
[09:55] Jamie Park: Yes, we offer onboarding support — we'll include a handover and 1-week on-call in the pilot SOW.
[10:03] [10:03] Samir Patel: Okay, that's helpful. A few nitty-gritty questions later, but overall this addresses our main concerns.
[10:10] Maya Chen: I have one more — does the console provide anomaly alerts for cost spikes?
[10:15] Ravi Kapoor: It does — anomaly detection triggers and optional alerting to Slack or PagerDuty. You can also configure spend caps per route to prevent runaway costs.
[10:26] Jamie Park: Alright let's recap next steps.
[10:30] Jamie Park: Action items: I'll send Dedicated pricing + security docs (SOC2, KMS, integration checklist). Ravi will run a per-route benchmark using your sample traces once you share them. Maya will send the traffic CSV and SLO targets. We'll schedule pilot kickoff for week of 2028-11-20.
[10:52] [10:52] Olivia Torres: Thanks — appreciate the demo. We'll review and get the traces over.
[10:57] Jamie Park: Perfect. We'll follow up via email with the SOW draft and links to the docs. Thanks everyone.

End transcript.
